title: BECE National Values Education: Civic Education - National Value Education - Election and Voter Responsibilities
exam: BECE National Values Education: Civic Education
subject: National Value Education

questions.q: How is an **Election** best defined in Civic Education?
options: A religious gathering meant strictly for praying for the country
The formal and constitutional process of decision-making by which a population chooses an individual to hold public office
A forceful takeover of government by heavily armed youths
A process where the oldest citizens naturally inherit political leadership
questions.explain: An **Election** is a formal, organized democratic procedure through which eligible citizens actively vote to choose their political leaders and representatives.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Civic Education
questions.subject: National Value Education

questions.q: Who among the following qualifies perfectly as a **Voter** in Nigeria?
options: A 16-year-old brilliant secondary school prefect
An adult citizen of a foreign country living in Lagos on a tourist visa
An 18-year-old Nigerian citizen who is officially registered and possesses a valid Permanent Voter's Card (PVC)
A highly successful politician who refuses to register with INEC
questions.explain: A **voter** is a legally eligible citizen (in Nigeria, 18 years and above) who has successfully undergone voter registration and possesses a PVC to participate in an election.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Civic Education
questions.subject: National Value Education

questions.q: There are different types of elections. What is a **Direct Election**?
options: An election where voters select delegates who will then vote for the actual candidates
An election where the military independently selects the winner directly
An election where the registered voters cast their ballots strictly and directly for the candidates of their choice
An election that is completely concluded within five minutes
questions.explain: In a **Direct Election**, the electorate votes personally and straight for the candidates they want in power, unlike an *indirect election* where they vote for delegates (an electoral college) who make the final choice.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Civic Education
questions.subject: National Value Education

questions.q: A Senator tragically dies in a car accident, leaving his legislative seat suddenly vacant before the end of his tenure. What type of election is constitutionally held to fill this sudden specific vacancy?
options: A Primary Election
A By-Election
A General Election
A Rerun Election
questions.explain: A **By-Election** is a special election held in a specific constituency strictly to fill a political vacancy that suddenly arises due to the death, resignation, or recall of an incumbent officeholder.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Civic Education
questions.subject: National Value Education

questions.q: Under the 1999 Constitution of Nigeria, what is the basic, non-negotiable **age qualification** for a citizen to be eligible to vote?
options: 16 years
18 years
21 years
30 years
questions.explain: Universal Adult Suffrage in Nigeria dictates that any sane citizen who has attained the minimum age of **18 years** is constitutionally eligible to register and vote.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Civic Education
questions.subject: National Value Education

questions.q: Which of the following describes a crucial pre-election **responsibility of a voter**?
options: Snatching the ballot box on election morning
Presenting oneself for formal registration with INEC to obtain a voter's card
Fighting political opponents physically during a campaign rally
Bribing electoral officers to secure favorable polling units
questions.explain: Before an election, it is a primary civic responsibility of a voter to undergo **voters' registration** and secure a valid Permanent Voter's Card (PVC) issued by INEC.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Civic Education
questions.subject: National Value Education

questions.q: Voting involves several rigorous steps on election day. What is the fundamental procedure a voter must first undergo upon arriving at a Polling Unit?
options: Casting the ballot paper straight into the box immediately upon arrival
Undergoing accreditation where the voter's identity and PVC are thoroughly verified by INEC officials
Lobbying party agents to get highly paid for voting
Publicly announcing the name of their preferred candidate to the crowd
questions.explain: The absolute first step of the voting procedure is **Accreditation**. During accreditation, INEC officials use devices (like the BVAS) to rigorously verify the voter's PVC, identity, and eligibility before they are given a ballot.
